title: Roommate-sharing app: 'not on violent-offender list' badge instead of a criminal record certificate
moment: A graduate student in Taipei wants to move into a shared 3-bedroom flat found through a roommate-matching group. The existing tenants ask every applicant to send a photo of their national ID plus a 良民證 (police criminal record certificate) over LINE, and the files stay in the group chat forever.
verifier: Existing tenants of the flat (private individuals, strangers to the applicant), via the matching platform
predicate: Applicant's identity (bound to a holder key) does not appear on the violent-offender register as of a stated date, and the proof is fresh (issued within 30 days)
disclosed_today: Full ID card photo (name, ID number, address, birthdate, photo) and a full 良民證 listing all record fields, kept indefinitely in chat history
issuer: National Police Agency criminal records unit, or Ministry of Justice, issuing a signed non-membership attestation through the TW DIW wallet
why_zk: The tenants need only a yes/no on one list; a non-membership proof stops strangers from holding a copy of the applicant's ID number and address, which is exactly what is later used for identity fraud. Weakness: the issuer must have a legal basis to expose a list-check service for private use, and a 'clean' result can be stale within days; the register itself may not be designed for citizen-initiated checks.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In tw-telco-online-id-check-fraud-2021, the provider accepts easily copied identifiers (ID number and issue date) as proof of who the applicant is; here, the holder-key binding of the signed attestation plays the role that replaces copyable ID details, so a stolen ID photo cannot pass the check.

In rd-twdiw-field-selection-consent, the wallet lets users pick fields to disclose per scenario with no field-level guarantee; here, a fixed single-predicate presentation request from the tenants plays the role that guarantees only the non-membership bit is released.

title: Carpool app driver check for a weekly Hsinchu science-park commute
moment: A software engineer joins a new weekday carpool from Taichung to Hsinchu Science Park. The group organiser asks each rider to post a selfie with ID and a screenshot of a police record, so the driver and three riders can feel safe sharing a car at 7am. The organiser keeps all of it in a shared Google Drive folder.
verifier: The carpool organiser (a peer) and the fellow riders, via the carpool app
predicate: Rider is not on the violent-offender list, shown once per group join, with a per-group pseudonym so the same person cannot be linked across different carpool groups
disclosed_today: Selfie with ID, full name, ID number, and a record screenshot, uploaded to a shared drive visible to all members
issuer: The carpool platform (e.g., a ride-sharing company) acting as a relying issuer after it checks the person once against the police service, then signing a reusable non-membership credential
why_zk: The riders need to trust a stranger for a short drive, not hold a dossier on them; a per-context proof avoids a shared folder that links a rider's real identity across groups. Weakness: if the platform is the issuer, riders rely on the platform's one-time check, and the credential does not prove anything about behaviour after issuance; unlinkability across groups also hides repeat complaints.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In an-a-samesite-cookies, a SameSite attribute stops a cookie being sent in cross-site requests so third parties cannot recognise the holder across sites; here, a per-group presentation pseudonym plays that role so one carpool group cannot match the rider to other groups.

In an-b-attorney-client, confidentiality breaks when an outsider is present unless essential to the relationship; here, the organiser's shared drive plays the outsider whose presence leaks the record, and the zero-knowledge presentation removes the need for any third party to see the underlying record.

title: Landlord-assisted room-share: sealed check done by the community, shown to a new flatmate
moment: A tenant in a Kaohsiung student apartment block wants to sublet one room to a stranger from a Facebook housing group. The previous flatmates insist that whoever moves in has been checked, but nobody wants to read another person's whole record or learn why a past record exists. A neighbourhood community management committee can do a one-off check.
verifier: The sitting tenants of the flat deciding on a sublet applicant, relying on the committee's signature
predicate: Applicant is not on the violent-offender list at the committee's check time, with the result kept hidden from everyone but the holder until the holder chooses to present it on move-in day
disclosed_today: Photocopy of the applicant's ID and 良民證, handed to the tenants and the community committee, with the committee office keeping a copy in its files
issuer: The community management committee (社區管理委員會) or a licensed housing agency, who obtains the applicant's own consented record query and signs a short-lived non-membership attestation
why_zk: Today the committee office holds copies of strangers' records that it has no reason to keep; a sealed attestation that the holder reveals only at move-in cuts that retention and stops the flatmates seeing record details. Weakness: a community committee is not an obviously trusted authority for criminal checks, and the legal permission to run such a check on behalf of private persons is unclear in Taiwan, so this idea is the weakest of the three.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-sealed-bid-far, the holder of sealed bids keeps them unopened until the scheduled moment and may handle the envelope only to identify it; here, the committee plays the holder who may confirm the attestation's identity and validity without opening the underlying record.

In an-b-jury-selection, a court keeps selected people's names confidential only as a judge-level exception to a default of publication; here, the committee's rule that the check result stays with the holder by default plays that protection, rather than relying on the committee's discretion to withhold.
